inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,795 logical lines of the normalized source. The recoverable prose develops the real/imaginary zero-curve X-ray as a representation of value, critical-point, zero-counting, Gram-point, Speiser, Lehmer, and Rosser phenomena; 26 materially distinct units are retained. Large figure-only runs preserve labels but not curve geometry in the text layer and are therefore accounted for as extraction-defective rather than interpreted. The late Hermite, Bessel, Airy, and Gamma comparison is readable but outside the Riemann-hypothesis scope of this plan. No v1 units were assigned.

accepted_units.title: Real and imaginary zero curves as a meromorphic X ray
accepted_units.why_material: The source's central representation change replaces a hard-to-see meromorphic map by the preimages of the real and imaginary axes, whose intersections expose zeros and poles and whose combined picture organizes scattered knowledge.
accepted_units.context_note: The opening mention of Speiser supplies the RH motivation, but the retained mechanism is the general curve representation stated in these lines.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete; thick-versus-thin styling is defined textually and no figure is needed to recover the mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Zeros, critical points, and monotonic motion on level curves
accepted_units.why_material: This span identifies curve intersections with zeta zeros, curve branching with derivative zeros, and monotonic variation of the remaining component along a regular real- or imaginary-value curve.
accepted_units.context_note: Concrete listed zeros illustrate the encoding but are not required for the reusable meromorphic-function mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose and derivative argument are recoverable; Figure 1 is illustrative only and its detailed geometry is not relied on.

accepted_units.title: Topological numbering of real- and imaginary-value lines
accepted_units.why_material: The author gives persistent integer identities to curves using their real-axis intersections and continuation, encoding parity as real versus imaginary value and allowing later geometric counting arguments.
accepted_units.context_note: The numbering excludes reflected curves below the real axis and is specific to the displayed zeta X ray.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose-complete; exact turns such as line 11 are figure-dependent examples and are not promoted beyond the stated observation.

accepted_units.title: Why imaginary-value curves disappear far to the right
accepted_units.why_material: Uniform convergence of zeta to 1 as real part grows gives a positive-real-part half-plane and therefore excludes purely imaginary values there.
accepted_units.context_note: The numerical boundary quoted by the source is not independently certified here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete.

accepted_units.title: Parallel line spacing and alternating zero carriage
accepted_units.why_material: Dominance of the first Dirichlet-series oscillation predicts nearly equally spaced real-value curves, while monotonic direction alternates so that every other regular parallel line is forced through zero.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusion is explicitly conditional on zeta-prime not vanishing along a line; the oval-surrounding exception shows why that regularity condition matters.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted leading-term formulas are legible enough to support the mechanism; Figure 2 is not required.

accepted_units.title: Orienting curve crossings by image quadrants
accepted_units.why_material: Following a real-value curve away from a zero determines the sign and limiting range of zeta and thereby assigns neighboring source-plane sectors to image-plane quadrants.
accepted_units.context_note: The worked orientation is local to the named curves but exemplifies a reusable conformal-map reading rule.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete; the subsequent diagram only illustrates the quadrant layout.

accepted_units.title: Curve boundaries partition the plane by image quadrant
accepted_units.why_material: The real- and imaginary-value curves form region boundaries, and crossing one boundary changes exactly one sign, enabling quadrant labels to propagate across the source plane.
accepted_units.context_note: The final named-line walk is an example of the general crossing rule.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete; Figure 3 is helpful but not necessary.

accepted_units.title: Counting solutions of zeta(s)=a from a region boundary
accepted_units.why_material: A region known to map into one quadrant is traversed on its curve boundary; the image winds twice around that quadrant, giving two preimages of any interior value and implying a derivative zero in the region.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact polygonal boundary names refer to Figure 4, but the table and prose state the winding calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Partly figure-dependent for the shape of the region; the boundary order, mapped ranges, winding count, and conclusion survive in text.

accepted_units.title: Computed curve tracing is not automatically proof
accepted_units.why_material: The source explains its numerical line-tracing construction and explicitly distinguishes proved exterior behavior from near-critical-strip paths accepted only after dense computation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a methodological limitation on the atlas, not a mathematical theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete.

accepted_units.title: From asymptotic line numbers to nontrivial-zero counts
accepted_units.why_material: Stirling's expansion and the functional equation number incoming curves, after which an argument-principle contour converts curve crossings into the classical main-term count of nontrivial zeros and a mod-four distinction between parallel-line types.
accepted_units.context_note: Formula extraction is imperfect around references to equations (2.1)-(2.3), so the conceptual bridge and stated nearest-integer relations are retained without repairing symbols from memory.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The contour sketch is partly interleaved with text, but its four sides, zero variation on three pieces, and crossing contribution on the fourth are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Euler-MacLaurin continuation with controllable remainder
accepted_units.why_material: The expansion represents zeta by a finite Dirichlet sum plus analytic correction terms and a bounded remainder, with tunable cutoffs yielding arbitrary precision throughout the plane.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit records the computational logic rather than asking a model to execute the formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula text is somewhat degraded but the decomposition and remainder-control claim are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Hardy's real transform and the Riemann-Siegel speedup
accepted_units.why_material: Multiplying critical-line zeta by a phase produces real Hardy Z, turning sign changes into certified critical-line zeros, while Riemann-Siegel reduces the dominant term count from order t to order square-root t.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical manuscript discussion after this span is context rather than a separate reusable mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core definitions, sign logic, error order, and complexity comparison are text-recoverable despite minor formula-layout damage.

accepted_units.title: Escape constraints force line pairing into sheets
accepted_units.why_material: A horizontal crossing bound prevents the many right-originating lines from escaping vertically through the strip; the much denser left family must pair and return, producing Speiser's sheets and increasingly nested configurations.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed integer sequence is observational and no prime-distribution connection is claimed by the author.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The forcing argument is prose-complete; particular nesting examples depend on the atlas.

accepted_units.title: Maintaining monotonicity through derivative zeros
accepted_units.why_material: At derivative zeros several level-curve branches meet; choosing an outgoing branch with the appropriate angle continues monotone function values, while non-polar curves must escape every compact set.
accepted_units.context_note: The local path of line 1187 is an example, not a globally verified reconstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The branch-continuation rule and compact-escape claim are readable; the motivating ambiguity is image-dependent.

accepted_units.title: First Speiser criterion via sheets meeting the critical line
accepted_units.why_material: Each real sheet carries exactly one zero by monotonicity and growth; the source uses how such a sheet intersects the critical line to formulate an RH-equivalent geometric condition.
accepted_units.context_note: This records the argument as presented. The source's own broader warning about geometric proofs and the atlas's computational status prevent treating the exposition alone as independent verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete.

accepted_units.title: Gram points turn phase regularity into sign brackets
accepted_units.why_material: Defining Gram points by integer phase makes zeta real there; the typical sign rule makes neighboring Hardy-Z values opposite and brackets critical-line zeros, while the mean-sign version still proves infinitely many such zeros without pointwise Gram's law.
accepted_units.context_note: The text explicitly anticipates exceptions, so the pointwise sign pattern is a tendency and Gram's law is not promoted as universal.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose and formulas are recoverable; Figures 13-14 only visualize separation.

accepted_units.title: Second Speiser criterion: derivative-zero separatrices
accepted_units.why_material: The source sketches how a left-of-line zeta zero forces a returning constant-argument separatrix through a derivative zero, and conversely how descending branches from a derivative zero set up a trapped region.
accepted_units.context_note: The author explicitly labels Speiser's method as gap-bearing and points to a flawless stronger result elsewhere; this unit is a strategic proof sketch, not a verified proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete through the setup of the reverse implication.

accepted_units.title: The trapped-region contradiction in the reverse Speiser direction
accepted_units.why_material: The increasing-modulus branch cannot cross either decreasing-modulus boundary or the critical-line segment, so assuming no left-side zeta zero leaves it unable to exit a bounded region.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the conclusion of the reverse-direction setup at lines 1102-1115; the intervening page is a figure and must not be mistaken for missing prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The closing obstruction is prose-complete but depends on the earlier region construction.

accepted_units.title: Derivative zeros organize near-intersections and sheet motion
accepted_units.why_material: Observed attraction of real curves toward derivative zeros explains sheet trajectories and abrupt near-crossings, including the distinction between exact perpendicular meeting at a real critical value and an almost-real near miss.
accepted_units.context_note: The claims about particular plotted zeros are graphical/computational observations, not independently certified here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conceptual local geometry is stated in prose; locations and line-specific diagnoses depend on the figures.

accepted_units.title: Sheet counts predict the number of derivative zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Subtracting alternating non-sheet zeros from the total zero count yields an asymptotic sheet count; under the one-critical-point-per-sheet interpretation this becomes the asymptotic count for zeros of zeta-prime.
accepted_units.context_note: The source clearly marks the geometric identification as conditional before citing an external proof of the resulting count.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The subtraction formula is legible enough to recover the counting logic.

accepted_units.title: Gram failures compensate in pairs and sheets restore correspondence
accepted_units.why_material: The first failure of Gram's law leaves one interval empty and the next doubly occupied, motivating a sheet-based bijection between Gram points and zeros rather than interval-by-interval order.
accepted_units.context_note: The resulting permutation is stated as well defined only under RH, and the bounded-displacement estimate is reported rather than proved here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exception counts and sheet reframing are prose-complete; exact drawn paths are figure-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Lehmer's close zeros expose cancellation and certification limits
accepted_units.why_material: A pair of extremely close zeros produces a tiny positive local maximum of Hardy Z through cancellation among Riemann-Siegel terms; changing its sign would signal an RH counterexample, and higher-precision Euler-MacLaurin evaluation is needed to separate the roots.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a historically computed near-failure, not evidence that RH fails.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Numerical values and mechanism are readable; the subsequent figures are not needed for the cancellation point.

accepted_units.title: Near-double-zero geometry and reconnection off the critical line
accepted_units.why_material: Two close zeros look like a double zero at coarse scale; the actual curves turn sharply near a derivative zero, and a small counterfactual reconnection would create a symmetric pair of off-line zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The modification is explicitly hypothetical and supplies a structural picture of instability, not a proof of realizability.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose states the reconnection; its visual plausibility depends on Figures 17-18.

accepted_units.title: Rosser blocks and S(t) quantify stronger failures of zero separation
accepted_units.why_material: Good and bad Gram points form blocks whose expected zero count is Rosser's law; the discrepancy S(t) measures departure from the smooth zero count, with thresholds explaining when Gram's and Rosser's rules can fail.
accepted_units.context_note: The threshold statements are reported by the source, and unbounded S makes any universal low-threshold regularity untenable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions and count relations are prose/formula complete; the concrete first counterexample is figure-supported.

accepted_units.title: Horizontal X-ray crossings encode the argument discrepancy
accepted_units.why_material: A large value of S is read as repeated real/imaginary curve crossings along a horizontal segment; tracking quadrant transitions reconstructs an argument change consistent with the numerical discrepancy.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact order of crossings is asserted from the plotted counterexample and should be scan-verified if used as item-level evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong figure dependency for the concrete crossing order; the quadrant-transition calculation is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Unbounded S predicts arbitrarily many-line coils
accepted_units.why_material: The source converts Selberg's unbounded discrepancy result into a qualitative prediction that higher X rays contain coils involving arbitrarily many level curves.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an extrapolated geometric expectation from the cited growth result, not direct observed evidence at all scales.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-complete; Figures 20 and 22 provide only the finite analogies.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Level-curve semantics as a topological computation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Preimages of the coordinate axes turn analytic value information into oriented regions, and boundary winding then counts preimages and forces critical points.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The concrete region geometry in the source is partly figure-dependent; only the text-stated crossings and winding should be used without scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Asymptotic line structure becomes a zero-counting instrument
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Right- and left-side asymptotics give persistent curve labels and spacing, while an argument-principle contour converts their crossings and parity into nontrivial-zero counts.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several displayed formulas have extraction damage, so exact constants require checking the retained original before training-item use.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Sheets recast RH as global curve connectivity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Escape constraints pair real-value curves into sheets, each carrying one zero; whether every sheet reaches the critical line supplies a global connectivity view of RH.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The atlas contains computed, not uniformly proved, near-strip paths, and the source exposition is not independent formal verification of the equivalence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Derivative zeros are the switching points of global topology
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Critical points permit level curves and constant-argument paths to turn, reconnect, or exchange apparent partners, making zeta-prime zeros the local organizers behind Speiser obstructions and Lehmer-style near-instability.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The second Speiser proof is explicitly gap-bearing and particular near-crossings are graphical observations.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zero-separation laws form a controlled hierarchy of breakdown
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Gram signs give local brackets, paired exceptions preserve nearby total counts, Rosser blocks weaken the regularity claim, and S(t) measures when increasingly elaborate crossing coils defeat each level.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Historical computations are pretraining-familiar and solver-independent mathematical novelty must not be inferred from reproducing this narrative.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Numerical representations need an explicit trust boundary
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Fast phase-normalized evaluation exposes sign changes, while controllable continuation and precision escalation are needed near tightly spaced zeros; dense plotted traces remain computational evidence unless separately certified.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source states available remainder bounds but this plan does not reproduce a certified implementation or verify the reported computations.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for recoverable RH-relevant semantic depth: every prose mechanism, theorem sketch, computational comparison, obstruction, counterexample pattern, and explicit evidence limitation is represented. Further units would predominantly duplicate the retained mechanisms, depend on curve geometry lost from image-only extraction, cover the out-of-scope special-function appendix, or reproduce bibliography/front matter.
stop_reason: The source ends after a comparative special-function appendix and references. All 1,795 lines have a disposition; remaining unselected RH-adjacent content consists of atlas images whose paths are not recoverable from normalized text, short transitions, repeated plotted examples, or a value-distribution aside not developed into the source's RH mechanisms. No unit quota was used.
